    parsed = []
    for item in items:
        title = item.find('h4').get_text()
        url = item.find('a')['href']

# Gender Roles in Modern Society

Gender roles have helped to shape society for centuries and have changed over time. With modern advancements in technology, science, and transportation, people have been able to better understand the world and their place in it. This has also led to a shift in gender roles, as women and men have begun to take on new roles in society.

One of the most common gender roles in modern society is the idea that women should be the primary caregivers for children, while men should be the primary breadwinners for their families. This role is still deeply ingrained in many cultures and can be seen in the way that men and women are portrayed in the media, from advertisements to movie roles.

However, the idea of gender roles being "fixed" is outdated. In reality, gender roles are fluid and constantly changing. Women are now able to take on roles that were once reserved for men, such as being presidents, CEOs, or scientists. Men are also now able to take on roles that were once thought to be exclusive to women, such as being stay-at-home parents or caring for elderly family members.

As society continues to evolve, it is important for us to recognize that gender roles should not be a limiting factor in our lives. Everyone should have the freedom to pursue their passions and dreams, regardless of gender. We should also be careful not to perpetuate stereotypes about men and women, as this can be harmful to both genders and to society as a whole.

In the end, gender roles should be a personal choice, not a societal obligation. People should have the freedom to choose their own path and define their own identity.

Consider talking to a therapist or counselor who can provide a neutral, non-judgmental space to explore your feelings and thoughts. They can help you clarify what's really bothering you and work through any underlying issues.

Focusing on self-care, like getting enough rest, eating well, and doing things that bring you joy, can also help you feel more balanced and centered. Taking time for yourself can give you the emotional space to process your feelings and make decisions from a place of clarity rather than anger.

Communicate with your husband about your feelings, using "I" statements and avoiding blame. Express what you need and want from the relationship. Try to listen to his perspective as well and find common ground where possible.

Couples counseling can also be helpful for working through challenges and rebuilding connection. Seek a licensed therapist who specializes in relationships for a collaborative, confidential space.

Remember that your well-being and happiness matter. You don't have to stay in a relationship that's not meeting your needs or making you feel bad about yourself. Seek out support and don't hesitate to reach out for help if you're struggling.
